summary: The UK government says Liechtenstein follows Schengen area rules. EU nationals have the right to travel freely in Liechtenstein, a non-EU member of the Schengen area. Under Regulation (EU) 2018/1806 (consolidated to 30 December 2025), nationals of the countries in its Annex II are exempt from the visa requirement for stays of no more than 90 days in any 180-day period, and nationals of the countries in Annex I must hold a visa; Liechtenstein's Immigration and Passport Office says visa-required people can apply at the Swiss representation where they live.

driving.text: Liechtenstein is a party to the 1949 Geneva and the 1968 Vienna Conventions on Road Traffic (UN Treaty Collection). Liechtenstein's Traffic Admission Ordinance (VZV, Art. 39) says drivers from abroad may drive motor vehicles if they hold a valid national driving licence, or a valid international driving permit under one of the listed conventions shown together with the national licence. Either entitles the holder to drive the categories documented on it explicitly, understandably and in Latin script. Under the Traffic Rules Ordinance (VRV, Art. 2), a blood-alcohol concentration of 0.8 per mille or more is in every case proof of unfitness to drive. Article 2a prohibits driving under the influence of alcohol, meaning a blood-alcohol concentration of 0.10 per mille or more, in licensed or cross-border passenger transport by road, in professional passenger transport, in goods transport with heavy motor vehicles, when carrying dangerous goods in transport units that must be marked, for driving instructors at work, for drivers on learner and practice drives, and for persons accompanying learner drives. Canada's travel advice says you can drive in Liechtenstein with a valid Canadian driver’s licence, although some car rental agencies may require an International Driving Permit; the UK government says you can drive with a UK driving licence and do not need an international driving permit (IDP). No official source we could read states how long a visitor may drive on a foreign licence.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Liechtenstein?
faq.answer: The UK government says Liechtenstein follows Schengen area rules, and EU nationals have the right to travel freely there. Under Regulation (EU) 2018/1806 (consolidated to 30 December 2025), nationals of the countries in its Annex II are exempt from the visa requirement for stays of no more than 90 days in any 180-day period; the UK tells British nationals they can travel to the Schengen area, which includes Liechtenstein, without a visa for up to 90 days in any 180-day period. Nationals of the countries in Annex I must hold a visa.

faq.question: Does Liechtenstein issue its own visas?
faq.answer: Liechtenstein's Immigration and Passport Office says visa-required people can apply at the Swiss representation where they live abroad, and that the decision lies partly with the Swiss authorities and partly with the Office. It lists places where the Swiss representation is not responsible for issuing visas for Liechtenstein, for example Tirana and Kuala Lumpur (Austria) and Chicago (Lithuania).

faq.question: Does time in Liechtenstein count toward my 90 Schengen days?
faq.answer: The UK government says British nationals can travel without a visa to the Schengen area, which includes Liechtenstein, for up to 90 days in any 180-day period, and that if you are travelling to other Schengen countries as well, your whole visit must be within the 90-day visa-free limit.

faq.question: What currency does Liechtenstein use?
faq.answer: The Swiss franc (CHF), according to Canada's travel advice.

Motorfahrzeugführer aus dem Ausland dürfen in Liechtenstein nur Motorfahrzeuge führen, wenn sie: a) einen gültigen nationalen Führerausweis besitzen; b) einen gültigen internationalen Führerausweis nach einem der folgenden Abkommen besitzen und einen solchen zusammen mit dem entspre- chenden nationalen Führerausweis vorweisen können:

Der ausländische nationale, der internationale Führerausweis zusammen mit dem nationalen Führerausweis oder der ausländische Lern- fahrausweis berechtigt den Inhaber in Liechtenstein zur Führung der Motorfahrzeugkategorien, die auf dem Ausweis ausdrücklich, verständlich und in lateinischer Schrift dokumentiert sind.
Fahrunfähigkeit wegen Alkoholeinwirkung (Angetrunkenheit) gilt in jedem Fall als erwiesen, wenn der Fahrzeugführer eine Blutalkohol-Kon- zentration von 0.8 oder mehr Gewichtspromillen aufweist
